title: dockato: water onto water, answers from standard input
purpose: `dockato` [@epsrmanual] builds larger molecules from `.ato` building blocks: copies of the first molecule of a docking file are bonded onto free sites of a docked file, removing one atom of each to form the new bond. This case chains water molecules and reads the docked-site parameters from standard input.
fortran: `dockato.f`: `dockato` (driver, parameters from command line or stdin), `rotatem`, `random_rotatem`, `search_unsaturated`, `find_valence`
system: The building block `WaterMolecule.ato` of EPSR-test: one water molecule (O1, H1, H1; O-H 0.976 Å, H-H 1.54 Å, SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charges [@berendsen1987]) in a 14.42 Å box at 300 K. Atom `atomd` of the new molecule is placed on `atomv`, the molecule is rotated so that its `atomdr` neighbour lies on the `atomvr` neighbour of `atomv` (equal bond lengths required), an optional second (dihedral) rotation about the new bond uses `atomdrr`/`atomvrr` (random angle in [dminrr, dmaxrr] from `ran1`, the Park-Miller generator with Bays-Durham shuffle [@parkmiller1988,@numrec1992], or a fixed dihedral that creates a DIH group when dminrr = dmaxrr), overlaps are tested with a distance factor, `atomd` and `atomvr` are removed and the new rotational group, bonds and atom types are updated. Here the docking H1 goes onto the docked O1 and the docking O1 onto the docked H1, so both H atoms are removed and an O-O bond is formed: a chain of water units joined by O-O bonds (a test structure, not a real molecule), with new ROT groups and the box rescaled.
inputs: Docking parameters on the command line (`H1 O1 H1`, radmax 10); run 1: `O1 H1 H1`, dihedral 30-90°, overlap factor 1.0 and output name from `dock_random.stdin`, 3 molecules; run 2: `dock_yes.stdin` with -60-60°, `yes` (overlaps allowed), a blank line before the output name (re-prompt) and the name given with `.ato`, 6 molecules.
verification: Each run writes one new `.ato` file (coordinates, bonds, rotational groups, atom types and the random-number state), compared byte for byte with the stored Fortran output. The overlap test is active: `waterchain.ato` holds 5 atoms (3 + 1 per docking), i.e. 2 of 3 placements accepted, with 2 ROT groups and box side 21.90 Å; `waterchain_yes.ato` has 9 atoms, 6 ROT groups (all 6 dockings) and box side 36.72 Å.
